we have reconstituted the complete transmembranal signaling of the DcuSR system in vitro, including the phosphorylation of DcuS by fumarate and the phosphorylation of the response regulator DcR by phosphorylated DcuS.
we have established a defined in vitro two-component system from Escherichiacoli, the DcuSR system, that is able to transmit signals across the membrane.

the DcuSR system ofEscherichiacoli controls expression of genes involved in C4-dicaboxylate metabolism inresponse to C4-dicarbxylate stimuli such as fumaric acid or succinic acid, and that DcuS functions as a Fumaric acid-stimulated histidine kinase in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of bacterial adaptation to the presence of C4-dioxygenase in the environment.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of signal transduction across the membrane in bacterial chemoreception.
understanding the function of the DcuSR signal transduction system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
His6-DcuSR is a fumarate-stimulating histidine protein kinase in vitro.
the DcuS histidine protein kinase is activated by fumarate and phosphorylates DcuR, the cognate response regulator.
the reconstitutionsystem represents the minimal in vitro system for the transmembrane signal transfer by DcuSR from the stimulus (C4-dicarboylates) to the DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the DcuSR system from E. coli is the first two-component system that is capable of signal transduction in vitro, including signal transfer from the extracellular stimulus to the DNA, and that the signal transfer across the membrane occurs by the DcuS protein, which has a sensory domain on the extracellular side of the membrane and a kinase domain on the cytoplasmatic side.
DcuS is able to sense the extracellular C4-dicaboxylates fumarate and succinate, and to transmit this information across the cytoplasmatic membrane.
the DcuS protein is a fumarate- stimulated His kinase in vitro, which phosphorylates the cognate response regulator DcuS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the DcuS histidine protein kinase is able to autophosphorylate in the presence of liposomes and ATP.
we have developed a reconstituted two-component system in vitro, which allows the complete signal transduction by a two-component regulatory system from stimulus to the DNA.
the DcuS kinase is capable of autophosphorylating and phosphorylating DcuR, and this phosphorylation is stimulated by fumarate.
